Three design directions for Malbec Ventures

Each one is the real site with a different palette, typeface and shape language applied, not a mock-up. The words, charts and layout are identical, so what you are comparing is only the look. Portfolio and LP figures shown are the current placeholders.

A · EstateB · GalleryC · Night harvest

My recommendation

A · Estate for the public site, B · Gallery for the LP site. The public site is a first impression, where being remembered matters most, and Estate is the only one of the three that no other fund could have made. The LP site is read closely by people comparing funds, where white pages and plain numerals are easiest to trust and to read at length. The two share the Malbec red and the logo, so they still feel like one firm.

If you want a single look across both, choose B. Choose C if matching your presentation decks matters more to you than reading comfort.

Feel
Editorial and warm, like a wine label. This is the look both sites have today, with the gold darkened slightly so small labels read clearly.
Type
Playfair Display for headings, with italics for emphasis. Inter for body text.
Shapes
Hairline rules, soft corners, full-width vineyard photograph in the hero.
Best for
Standing out from other funds. Nobody else in Israeli or Latin American venture looks like this, and it carries the Malbec story without explanation.
Watch out for
Serif-and-cream can read as boutique or lifestyle to an institutional LP. Dense data pages feel a little soft.

Feel
Crisp, modern and numbers-first. White pages, near-black text, Malbec red used sparingly, navy for data. The red and navy are the two colours already in your email signature.
Type
Inter Tight, bold, for headings. Inter for body text. No italics: emphasis is carried by colour.
Shapes
Square corners, thin borders, generous white space. The hero is type on white with the photograph contained in a frame.
Best for
Experienced LPs and anything with numbers. Reads like a well-made investor report; the most familiar to people who see many funds.
Watch out for
The least distinctive of the three. The warmth of the wine story has to come from the words and the photograph, not the page. The LP sidebar stays navy in this version rather than white.

Feel
Confident and dramatic, built for big numbers. It is the ground colour of your own Embassy deck, taken to a full site, with amber for the orange and rose for the grape.
Type
Sora, bold, for headings. Inter for body text.
Shapes
Filled tiles with rounded corners, stat cards throughout, the hero photograph under a navy wash.
Best for
Presenting on a screen in a room, and matching your decks exactly. Big figures land hardest here.
Watch out for
Long reading (terms, legal, DD questionnaire) is more tiring on dark. Portfolio logos need white chips behind them. Prints poorly.
Prepared for Hagai Platin. Screens are from a local build; nothing is live. The LP screens contain confidential material: please do not forward this page.
